decision: Determine whether model scale is the binding constraint, or whether the task/data/metric contract prevents stronger models from clearing semantic thresholds.

A_tiny_baseline.model: repo tiny TwoTower scratch baseline (e714 recipe, 600 steps, symbol-only output contract v2)
A_tiny_baseline.checkpoint: trained fresh under the run cap from outputs/data/train/slm230_symbol_only_v1; claim_class=diagnostic (scratch, not a ship candidate)

B_smollm2_135m.revision: pinned at execution time and recorded per arm
B_smollm2_135m.decode: greedy (temperature 0), max_new_tokens 384, prompt template published in the run manifest; official parser post-validation (legality measured, not enforced)

C_qwen25_7b.revision: pinned at execution time and recorded per arm
C_qwen25_7b.decode: identical template and decoding parameters as arm B

frozen_requests.source: outputs/data/test built from src/slm_training/resources/rico/semantic_test.jsonl via scripts/build_test_data (leakage-filtered vs train manifests)
frozen_requests.sha256: recorded at freeze time in the run manifest

metrics.primary: binding_aware_meaningful_v2_rate_strict (candidate_pending_calibration; deterministic fail-closed, no LLM judge)
secondary: meaningful_program_v1_report verdict rate + typed reason-code histogram (diagnostic-only per SLM-288 demotion)
metrics.human_subset: the SLM-288 frozen packet is output-labels of prior generations and does not transfer to new arm outputs; the three smoke prompts it covers are included in analysis as a secondary stratum with agent-rater labels relabeled blind per arm output (disclosed non-human)

thresholds.scale_binding: arm C primary-metric Wilson lower bound exceeds arm A Wilson upper bound by >= 0.10 AND arm C syntax/validity >= arm A
thresholds.task_or_metric_binding: arm C primary-metric Wilson upper bound <= 0.10 (even a 7B external model cannot clear semantic thresholds) OR arm C Wilson upper bound <= arm A Wilson lower bound + 0.10 (no scale effect)
thresholds.inconclusive: any other outcome, any arm incomplete (e.g. 7B infeasible under the run policy), or any evidence-bar violation

cost_cap.chunked_resume: arms run in <=170s chunks with deterministic resume; a timed-out or killed chunk is never evidence

claim_rules.leakage: prompts contain prompt-visible inputs only; no gold openui, placeholders inventory, or evaluator fields in prompts (checked by a prompt-audit test)
claim_rules.evidence: raw outputs persisted per arm + EvidenceBundleV1 (SLM-291) before disposition; AgentEvals JSONL + AgentV bundle (claim diagnostic)

lar_consequences.scale_binding: LAR2-LAR4 architecture program preserved; scale is the binding lever
lar_consequences.task_or_metric_binding: LAR2-LAR4 architecture program closes; task/data/metric contract must change first
lar_consequences.inconclusive: LAR2-LAR4 remain blocked pending the named resolving evidence

amendments.change: arm A decode: unconstrained generation + official post-validation (identical to arms B/C) instead of canonical grammar-constrained decode
amendments.evidence: grammar-constrained LTR decode costs >20s/token on rico-scale layouts (stuck in lark LALR accepts() per candidate token; a single request exceeds the 170s command cap). Unconstrained decode: 256 tokens in 11.0s on the same checkpoint. Constraining is therefore infeasible under the run policy for every arm; uniform unconstrained+post-validation is the fair comparison and legality is still measured via the official parser.
amendments.also: arm A training uses chunked --resume-from under the 170s command cap (~15s/step on this corpus; the first 600-step attempt was wall-capped at 12 steps and is discarded)

amendments.change: arm C loads bfloat16 instead of float32 (same greedy decode/template; host RAM cannot hold a 7B fp32 copy)
amendments.evidence: fp32 load of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct drove host RAM to 0 GB available and the chunk was killed before producing any output.

amendments.change: evaluated request set fixed to the deterministic first-20 prefix of the 35 frozen requests; max_new_tokens 384 -> 256; execution serialized one request per command inside the 170s policy cap
amendments.evidence: measured latency under memory contention was 661-1700s/request (SmolLM2-135M), breaching both the 170s command cap and the locked 240 CPU-minute per-arm cap at n=35. n=20 still meets the LAR0 minimum (DEFAULT_MIN_SUITE_N=20). All outputs produced by over-cap commands were discarded, not scored.

amendments.change: arm C (Qwen2.5-7B) declared not_run under local policy unless an uncontended single request completes within 170s; otherwise the disposition is inconclusive with arm C as the resolving evidence
amendments.evidence: 7B bf16 CPU generation is projected at several minutes per request even uncontended (measured fp32 OOM; no local GPU; HF_TOKEN unset so managed HF Jobs unavailable).

amendments.change: arm B (SmolLM2-135M) also declared not_run under local policy: a single uncontended fp32 request took 296s (>170s cap); bf16 projection still exceeds the cap; reducing max_new_tokens to fit was rejected because truncating external outputs while arm A gets full length would bias the scale comparison. All over-cap outputs discarded unscored.
amendments.evidence: measured 2026-07-24: 4m56s for one 256-token greedy request, model load ~30s, 12-core CPU host; user time 14m41s.

amendments.change: arm A decode also not_run: the trained 600-step checkpoint's constrained decode costs >17s/token on rico-scale layouts (>280s for 16 tokens; lark lexer rebuild per token in compiler_draft.build_completion_forest). Arm A TRAINING completed within policy (600 steps, final loss 1.5187, chunked resume under the 170s cap). No request of any arm completed within the cap on this host; every over-cap output was discarded unscored.
amendments.evidence: faulthandler traces 2026-07-24 (models/grammar.py pick_constrained_token -> compiler_draft build_completion_forest -> lark _build_lexer); fresh-untrained model decodes the same record in 8.5s/64 tokens while the trained checkpoint exceeds 280s/16 tokens.
